verdict.rationale: Outlook's own documented Inbox rules, which apps can set up via Graph, automatically act on incoming messages, for example by forwarding them. That is a direct rule-triggered-action capability. However, the evidence covers only one event type (message arrival) in brief one-line mentions, with no detail on conditions or actions and no hands-on corroboration. Change-notification subscriptions are an alerting building block, not rules that trigger actions, so they are not credited. missing for 10: documented rule conditions and action catalog, rules triggered by events beyond incoming mail (e.g. calendar), in-depth docs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Apps can set up [Inbox rules](/en-us/graph/api/resources/messagerule) to promptly handle incoming messages and reduce email clutter.
Use Inbox rules to automate actions such as forwarding specific incoming messages
